manual.mchjong.entry.companions.name: Inviting Companions
manual.mchjong.entry.companions.page_1: Pick online friends from the lobby sidebar or Room Settings → Invite, or run /mchjong invite <player> in chat. Guests must stand within 6 blocks of the table and accept within 60 seconds.
manual.mchjong.entry.companions.page_1.c: The host can also add bots to fill open seats. Riichi offers Easy or Hard bots. MCR, Sichuan, and Taiwan each provide a dedicated built-in bot.
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.name: Discards & Controls
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.page_1: By default, click a tile in your hand to discard it. Choose Single Click, Double Click, or Select + Confirm as your discard method in Personal Settings.
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.page_1.con: Shift-click to select without discarding. Click Discard to confirm the selected tile.
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.page_1_con: Use the buttons beside your hand to declare riichi, pass, call Chi, Pon or Kan, or win. Right-click or press Esc to cancel your selection.
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.page_2: Use the view button to switch between seated and immersive views. Right-drag to look around and scroll to move closer or farther away.
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.page_2.con: Reset the view in Personal Settings. To stand up, press Esc to close the screen, then sneak.
manual.mchjong.entry.customization.name: Appearance & Audio
manual.mchjong.entry.customization.page_: Put Mahjong Dye in the box’s dye slot to preview tile-face and tile-back presets. Click Apply to use both presets, consuming one dye.
Vanilla dyes recolor tile backs directly. Reprinting a whole set erases the red marks on red fives. If your rules use red dora, reapply Red Dora Dye after printing.
Personal Settings lets you adjust camera distance, draw-and-discard animation speed and volume. Custom riichi sticks and voices are chosen in Personal Presets.
Put custom ZIP packs in config/mchjong/presets under faces, backs, sticks, or voices. Presets download automatically when you join a server that shares them.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.name: Placing the Table
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.page_1: Clear a flat 3 × 3 area with nothing above it and a solid block directly beneath the center.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.page_1.co: Place stools two blocks away from the center on each side you intend to play on. Lay a tablecloth first, then put a mahjong box with a complete set inside the table.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.page_2: Craft the table from matching wooden slabs and fences, and add a white carpet to make each stool. Three carpets of the same color in a row fold into a tablecloth.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.page_2.co: Right-click the table with a cloth in hand to drape it, then right-click again to open storage and insert the box.
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.name: Table Operation
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.page_1: Riichi mahjong ordinary tables are fully hands-on, close to a real table. The dealer sweeps the tiles to shuffle, then everyone drags loose tiles in front of themselves to build a wall.
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.page_1.con: Once the walls are up, the dealer picks up the dice from the center and rolls to open the wall.
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.page_1_con: Deal your hand by dragging highlighted tile packets toward your hand. Take four tiles in each of three rounds, then one more tile each.
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.page_2: The dealer takes the extra 14th tile to start. Drag the highlighted tiles from the wall to draw. Press Esc to cancel a drag.
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.page_2.con: Upgrade the table at a crafting table with iron ingots, redstone dust, copper ingots, and a hopper. The automatic table then shuffles, builds walls, deals, and draws on its own.
manual.mchjong.entry.maid.name: Touhou Little Maid
manual.mchjong.entry.maid.page_1: With Touhou Little Maid installed on both the server and the client, you can assign a maid the Mahjong task. Keep an equipped table with an empty stool inside her work area, and take your seat first.
manual.mchjong.entry.maid.page_1.continu: During work hours she comes over, sits down, and follows the seat assignment. Switching her task makes her stand up and leaves the seat free.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.name: High-Scoring Patterns
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.page_1: $(bold)Big Four Winds$()$(br)88 fan$(br2)The hand contains a pung or kong of each of the four winds. Do not add Big Three Winds, Prevalent Wind, Seat Wind, Pung of Terminals or Honors, or All Pungs for these groups.
$(bold)Little Three Dragons$()$(br)64 fan$(br2)The hand contains pungs or kongs of two dragons and a pair of the third dragon. Do not add Two Dragon Pungs or Dragon Pung.
$(bold)All Honors$()$(br)64 fan$(br2)The hand consists entirely of honor tiles. Do not add All Pungs, Outside Hand, Pung of Terminals or Honors, or One Voided Suit.

$(bold)Four Concealed Pungs$()$(br)64 fan$(br2)The hand contains four concealed pungs or kongs. A pung completed with another player’s discard does not count as concealed. Do not add All Pungs or Concealed Hand. A self-drawn win also scores Fully Concealed Hand.

$(bold)Pure Terminal Chows$()$(br)64 fan$(br2)The hand contains two 123 chows, two 789 chows, and a pair of fives, all in one suit. Do not add Full Flush, All Chows, Pure Double Chow, Two Terminal Chows, or No Honors.
$(bold)Quadruple Chow$()$(br)48 fan$(br2)The hand contains four identical chows in one suit. Do not count the same tiles again as Pure Triple Chow, Pure Double Chow, or Tile Hog.
$(bold)Four Pure Shifted Pungs$()$(br)48 fan$(br2)The hand contains four pungs of consecutive numbers in one suit. Do not add Pure Shifted Pungs or All Pungs.

$(bold)Four Pure Shifted Chows$()$(br)32 fan$(br2)The hand contains four chows in one suit. Their starting numbers increase by one each time or by two each time. Do not also count Pure Shifted Chows formed from three of these chows.

$(bold)Three Kongs$()$(br)32 fan$(br2)The hand contains three kongs. Add 2 fan if one is concealed, or 8 fan if two are concealed. If all three are concealed, they can also qualify for Three Concealed Pungs.
$(bold)All Terminals And Honors$()$(br)32 fan$(br2)The hand consists entirely of terminals and honors. Do not add All Pungs, Outside Hand, or Pung of Terminals or Honors.

$(bold)Seven Pairs$()$(br)24 fan$(br2)The closed hand consists of seven pairs. Four identical tiles may form two pairs and also score Tile Hog. Do not add Concealed Hand or Single Wait. A self-drawn win also scores Fully Concealed Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.page_2: $(bold)Big Three Dragons$()$(br)88 fan$(br2)The hand contains a pung or kong of each of the three dragons. Do not add Two Dragon Pungs or Dragon Pung.

$(bold)Greater Honors And Knitted Tiles$()$(br)24 fan$(br2)The closed hand contains all seven different honors and seven suited tiles. Assign 147, 258, and 369 to different suits, then choose seven different tiles from that pattern. All fourteen tiles must be different. Do not add Lesser Honors And Knitted Tiles, All Types, or Concealed Hand.
$(bold)All Even Pungs$()$(br)24 fan$(br2)Every pung or kong and the pair consists of twos, fours, sixes, or eights. Do not add All Pungs, All Simples, or No Honors.
$(bold)Full Flush$()$(br)24 fan$(br2)The hand consists entirely of tiles from one numbered suit, with no honors. Do not add One Voided Suit or No Honors.
$(bold)Pure Triple Chow$()$(br)24 fan$(br2)The hand contains three identical chows in one suit. Do not count the same tiles again as Pure Shifted Pungs or Pure Double Chow.
$(bold)Pure Shifted Pungs$()$(br)24 fan$(br2)The hand contains three pungs of consecutive numbers in one suit. Do not count the same tiles again as Pure Triple Chow.
$(bold)Upper Tiles$()$(br)24 fan$(br2)The hand uses only sevens, eights, and nines. Do not add Upper Four or No Honors.
$(bold)Middle Tiles$()$(br)24 fan$(br2)The hand uses only fours, fives, and sixes. Do not add All Simples or No Honors.
$(bold)Lower Tiles$()$(br)24 fan$(br2)The hand uses only ones, twos, and threes. Do not add Lower Four or No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.page_3: $(bold)All Green$()$(br)88 fan$(br2)The hand uses only the 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 of bamboo and the Green Dragon. Full Flush or Half Flush may also score, as appropriate.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.page_4: $(bold)Nine Gates$()$(br)88 fan$(br2)The closed hand holds 1112345678999 in one suit, then wins on any tile of that suit. Do not add Full Flush or Concealed Hand. A self-drawn win also scores Fully Concealed Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.page_5: $(bold)Four Kongs$()$(br)88 fan$(br2)The hand contains four kongs and a pair. Do not add Single Wait. Concealed kongs can still qualify for the applicable concealed-kong or concealed-pung scoring patterns.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.page_6: $(bold)Seven Shifted Pairs$()$(br)88 fan$(br2)The closed hand consists of seven pairs with consecutive numbers, all in one suit. Do not add Seven Pairs, Full Flush, Concealed Hand, or Single Wait. A self-drawn win also scores Fully Concealed Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.page_7: $(bold)Thirteen Orphans$()$(br)88 fan$(br2)The closed hand contains one of each of the thirteen different terminals and honors, plus one extra tile to form a pair. A self-drawn win also scores Fully Concealed Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.page_8: $(bold)All Terminals$()$(br)64 fan$(br2)The hand uses only ones and nines. Do not add All Pungs, Outside Hand, Pung of Terminals or Honors, or No Honors. A separate Double Pung may also score.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.page_9: $(bold)Little Four Winds$()$(br)64 fan$(br2)The hand contains pungs or kongs of three winds and a pair of the fourth wind. Do not add Big Three Winds or Pung of Terminals or Honors for those groups.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.name: Basic Scoring Patterns
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_1: $(bold)Outside Hand$()$(br)4 fan$(br2)Every set and the pair in the winning hand contains at least one terminal or honor. The hand does not have to be concealed.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_10: $(bold)Tile Hog$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)The winning hand uses all four copies of one tile without declaring them as a kong. Count Tile Hog once for each tile type that meets this condition.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_11: $(bold)Double Pung$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)The hand contains pungs or kongs of the same number in two different suits. Do not add Double Pung for groups already counted as Triple Pung.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_12: $(bold)Two Concealed Pungs$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)The hand contains two concealed pungs or kongs. A pung completed with another player’s discard does not count as concealed.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_13: $(bold)Concealed Kong$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)Declare a kong using four identical tiles from your own hand. On winning, score it as Concealed Kong, without adding the point for Melded Kong.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_14: $(bold)All Simples$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)The winning hand uses only suited tiles numbered two through eight, with no terminals or honors. The hand may be open. Do not add No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_15: $(bold)Pure Double Chow$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)The hand contains two identical chows in one suit. If these chows are already included in a higher-scoring pattern that contains Pure Double Chow, do not count them again.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_16: $(bold)Mixed Double Chow$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)The hand contains chows of the same numbers in two different suits. If these chows are already included in a higher-scoring pattern that contains Mixed Double Chow, do not count them again.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_17: $(bold)Short Straight$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)The hand contains two chows of the same suit that join to form six consecutive numbers.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_18: $(bold)Two Terminal Chows$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)The hand contains a 123 chow and a 789 chow in the same suit.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_19: $(bold)Pung Of Terminals Or Honors$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)The hand contains a pung or kong of a one or nine, or of a wind that is neither the seat wind nor the round wind. A dragon pung or kong scores 2 fan for Dragon Pung instead. Do not also count it here.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_2: $(bold)Fully Concealed Hand$()$(br)4 fan$(br2)Win by self-draw without having called a chow, pung, or exposed kong. Concealed kongs are allowed. Do not add Concealed Hand or Self-Drawn.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_20: $(bold)Melded Kong$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)The hand contains a kong claimed from another player’s discard, or an added kong made by extending an exposed pung. Do not score that kong separately if it is already counted in a two-, three-, or four-kong pattern.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_21: $(bold)One Voided Suit$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)The winning hand is missing one of the three numbered suits. Do not add One Voided Suit when it is already included in Full Flush, Half Flush, or another scoring pattern.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_22: $(bold)No Honors$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)The winning hand contains no honors. Do not add No Honors when it is already included in All Chows, All Simples, Full Flush, or another scoring pattern.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_23: $(bold)Edge Wait$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)The hand can win only on a 3 completing 123, or a 7 completing 789. Do not count Edge Wait if there is another way to complete the hand. Count only one of Edge Wait, Closed Wait, and Single Wait.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_24: $(bold)Closed Wait$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)The hand can win only on the middle tile of a chow. Count only one of Closed Wait, Edge Wait, and Single Wait.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_25: $(bold)Single Wait$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)The hand waits on just one tile type to complete its pair. Do not add Single Wait when it is already included in Melded Hand, Four Kongs, Seven Pairs, or another scoring pattern.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_26: $(bold)Self-Drawn$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Win by drawing your own winning tile. Do not add this point if the hand already scores Fully Concealed Hand, Last Tile Draw, or Out With Replacement Tile.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_27: $(bold)Flower Tiles$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Each revealed flower adds 1 point. First meet the 8-fan minimum without flowers, then add the flower points. Flowers cannot help meet the minimum.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_3: $(bold)Two Melded Kongs$()$(br)4 fan$(br2)Two exposed kongs score 4 fan. One exposed kong and one concealed kong score 6 fan. In either case, do not add the points for the individual kongs.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_4: $(bold)Last Tile$()$(br)4 fan$(br2)Win on the fourth copy of a tile when the other three copies are already visible to all players. Tiles concealed in another player’s hand or still hidden in the wall do not count toward those three.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_5: $(bold)Dragon Pung$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)The hand contains a pung or kong of a dragon. Do not add Dragon Pung for a group already included in Two Dragon Pungs, Big Three Dragons, or Little Three Dragons.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_6: $(bold)Prevalent Wind$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)The hand contains a pung or kong of the round wind. If it is also your seat wind, add Seat Wind as well. Do not also score this group as Pung of Terminals or Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_7: $(bold)Seat Wind$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)The hand contains a pung or kong of your seat wind. If it is also the round wind, add Prevalent Wind as well.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_8: $(bold)Concealed Hand$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)Win on another player’s discard without having called a chow, pung, or exposed kong. Concealed kongs are allowed. A self-drawn win instead scores Fully Concealed Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.page_9: $(bold)All Chows$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)The winning hand consists of four chows and a pair of suited tiles. Called chows are allowed. Do not add No Honors. Unlike Pinfu in Riichi mahjong, this pattern does not require a two-sided wait.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.name: Mid-Range Scoring Patterns
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.page: $(bold)Pure Straight$()$(br)16 fan$(br2)The hand contains a 123 chow, a 456 chow, and a 789 chow in the same suit. Do not count those chows again as Short Straight or Two Terminal Chows.
$(bold)Lower Four$()$(br)12 fan$(br2)The hand uses only suited tiles numbered one through four. Do not add No Honors. If it uses only ones, twos, and threes, score Lower Tiles instead.

$(bold)Big Three Winds$()$(br)12 fan$(br2)The hand contains pungs or kongs of three different winds. Do not add Pung of Terminals or Honors for those groups. Add Prevalent Wind or Seat Wind if the corresponding wind is present.
$(bold)Mixed Straight$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)The hand contains a 123 chow, a 456 chow, and a 789 chow, each in a different suit.

$(bold)Reversible Tiles$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)The hand uses only tiles whose faces look the same upside down. These are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, and 9 of circles, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, and 9 of bamboo, and the White Dragon. Do not add One Voided Suit.
$(bold)Mixed Triple Chow$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)The hand contains a chow with the same numbers in each of the three suits. Do not count pairs of those chows again as Mixed Double Chow.
$(bold)Mixed Shifted Pungs$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)The hand contains three pungs of consecutive numbers, each in a different suit.

$(bold)Chicken Hand$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)A winning hand with no scoring pattern other than flowers scores 8 fan. Flower points are added separately. The illustrated hand is open and wins on a discarded 6 of circles, without Last Tile Claim or Last Tile.
$(bold)Last Tile Draw$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)Win by drawing the last tile from the wall. Do not also score Self Drawn.
$(bold)Last Tile Claim$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)Win on the discard made after the last tile is drawn from the wall. This is different from Last Tile, which concerns the fourth copy of a tile.
$(bold)Out With Replacement Tile$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)Win by drawing the replacement tile after a kong. Do not also score Self Drawn. A replacement drawn only for a flower does not qualify.

$(bold)Three-Suited Terminal Chows$()$(br)16 fan$(br2)Form a 123 chow and a 789 chow in each of two suits, with a pair of fives in the third suit. Do not also score All Chows, Mixed Double Chow, Two Terminal Chows, or No Honors.
$(bold)Robbing The Kong$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)Win on the fourth tile another player adds to an exposed pung to declare a kong. Do not also score Last Tile.

$(bold)All Pungs$()$(br)6 fan$(br2)Form four pungs or kongs and a pair. The hand may be open. Do not add its 6 fan to patterns that already include it, such as Big Four Winds, All Terminals, or All Honors.
$(bold)Half Flush$()$(br)6 fan$(br2)Use tiles from one numbered suit together with honors. Do not also score One Voided Suit.
$(bold)Mixed Shifted Chows$()$(br)6 fan$(br2)Form one chow in each suit, with starting numbers that increase by one from chow to chow.
$(bold)All Types$()$(br)6 fan$(br2)Include all three suits, a wind, and a dragon.
$(bold)Melded Hand$()$(br)6 fan$(br2)Expose all four groups by claiming other players’ discards, then win on a discard that completes the pair. Do not also score Single Wait.
$(bold)Two Concealed Kongs$()$(br)8 fan$(br2)Two concealed kongs score 8 fan. Do not also score either kong separately as Concealed Kong, or score the two together as Two Concealed Pungs.
$(bold)Two Dragon Pungs$()$(br)6 fan$(br2)Form pungs or kongs of two different dragons. Do not also score Dragon Pung for either group.
$(bold)Pure Shifted Chows$()$(br)16 fan$(br2)Form three chows in one suit. Their starting numbers must increase consistently by one, or consistently by two.
$(bold)All Fives$()$(br)16 fan$(br2)Each of the four groups and the pair must contain a five. Do not also score All Simples or No Honors.
$(bold)Triple Pung$()$(br)16 fan$(br2)Form a pung or kong of the same number in each of the three suits. Do not also score Double Pung from these groups.
$(bold)Three Concealed Pungs$()$(br)16 fan$(br2)Form three concealed pungs or concealed kongs. A pung completed by the winning discard counts as exposed. Do not also score Two Concealed Pungs.

$(bold)Lesser Honors And Knitted Tiles$()$(br)12 fan$(br2)Use fourteen distinct tiles drawn from honors and a pattern of 147 in one suit, 258 in another, and 369 in the third. The hand must be closed. Add Knitted Straight if all nine suited tiles are present, and Fully Concealed Hand if you win by self-draw.

$(bold)Knitted Straight$()$(br)12 fan$(br2)Use 147 in one suit, 258 in another, and 369 in the third, together with one group and a pair. Only the extra group may be exposed. The nine knitted tiles cannot be rearranged to score other patterns.
$(bold)Upper Four$()$(br)12 fan$(br2)Use only sixes, sevens, eights, and nines. Do not also score No Honors. If the hand contains only sevens, eights, and nines, score Upper Tiles instead.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.name: Flowers & Winning
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.page_1: MCR is played by four players with 136 ordinary tiles and eight flowers, for 144 tiles in all. You start with 13 tiles, or 14 as the dealer, who discards first.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.page_1.con: Turns move counterclockwise. Replace opening flowers dealer-first, one player at a time. Reveal each flower and replace it from the wall tail. Keep replacing if another flower appears.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.page_2: You may chow only the previous player’s discard. You may pung or declare an exposed kong using any opponent’s discard. A win takes priority over a pung or kong, which takes priority over a chow.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.page_2.con: If several players claim a win on the same discard, only the first in turn order after the discarder wins. Draw a replacement after a concealed kong.
Before completing an added kong, other players have a chance to rob it. Replacing a flower alone does not qualify for Out With Replacement Tile, and flowers cannot be used in groups.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.page_3: The regular shape is four groups and a pair. See $(l:mcr_special)Special Hands$(/l) for Seven Pairs, Thirteen Orphans, knitted forms, and Knitted Straight.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.page_3.con: You need eight non-flower points to win. Each flower adds one afterward. Seven points plus two flowers is still short. Eight points plus two flowers qualifies and pays as ten.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.page_4: MCR has no riichi, dora, or furiten. If you declare a win with a complete hand but fewer than eight non-flower points, it is a false win. Pay each opponent 10 points. You cannot win for the rest of that hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.page_4.con: You still draw, discard, and make calls normally. You may win again from the next hand. The Win button indicates a complete tile shape, so check that the scoring patterns reach eight points before declaring.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.page_5: On self-draw, each opponent pays eight plus the total hand score. On a discard, the discarder pays that amount and the other two pay eight each.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.page_5.con: For eight points plus two flowers, self-draw collects 18 each, for a total of 54. A discard collects 18, 8, and 8, for a total of 34. There is no dealer multiplier or fu.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.page_6: Start at zero points and play sixteen hands across the East, South, West, and North rounds. The dealer changes after every hand, including a dealer win or a draw. When the wall runs out, no payments are made for ready or not-ready hands.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.page_6.con: Any penalties already paid for a false win remain in effect. All 81 scoring patterns appear in $(l:mcr_fan_high)High-Scoring Patterns$(/l), $(l:mcr_fan_middle)Mid-Range Scoring Patterns$(/l), and $(l:mcr_fan_low)Basic Scoring Patterns$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.knitted: The nine tiles of a Knitted Straight, plus one group and a pair.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.kongs: These two kongs score six fan if one is exposed and one concealed.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.name: Shapes & Combinations
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.page_1: Seven Pairs uses fourteen tiles. Four identical tiles may count as two pairs. Thirteen Orphans uses one of each of the thirteen terminals and honors, plus a second copy of one of them.
Neither hand allows calls or kongs. For Lesser Honors and Knitted Tiles, select fourteen distinct tiles from honors and a pattern of 147 in one suit, 258 in another, and 369 in the third.
If all seven honors are present, score Greater Honors and Knitted Tiles instead. Both hands must be closed. Do not also score All Types or Concealed Hand. A self-draw adds Fully Concealed Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.page_2: Knitted Straight uses 147 in one suit, 258 in another, and 369 in the third, plus one group and a pair. The nine knitted tiles cannot be called as chows. Only the extra group may be exposed.
To score Edge Wait, Closed Wait, or Single Wait, the remaining group and pair must have only one winning tile type. Do not use any of the nine knitted tiles again when checking that wait. Another copy of the same tile may be used.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.page_3: Add scoring patterns that can be combined. Do not count a smaller pattern already included in a larger one, or count the same tiles again using a different arrangement.
For chow combinations, a group already used in one combination may combine once more with a group not yet used. Mixed Triple Chow does not also score Mixed Double Chow.

Pure Straight does not also score Short Straight or Two Terminal Chows from those same chows. If the hand has several possible arrangements, use the one with the highest score. Do not add the scores of different arrangements.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.page_4: The numbers in the index are the fan values of individual patterns. Ordinary patterns may be open unless marked as closed. The examples use Hong Kong tile faces.$(br2)+ marks the winning tile, / separates exposed groups from concealed tiles, and ; precedes tiles already revealed. Two concealed kongs score 8 fan. One exposed and one concealed kong score 6 fan. Do not score those kongs again separately.
manual.mchjong.entry.presets.name: Rules & Red Fives
manual.mchjong.entry.presets.page_1: The host picks a rule preset in the lobby. Hover any option to read its description. Settings cover red fives, starting points, game length, and bankruptcy. Changing rules resets everyone's readiness.
manual.mchjong.entry.presets.page_1.cont: Three-player mahjong drops 2m through 8m and plays with 108 tiles. North can stay in your hand as a normal tile or be extracted for an extra draw, depending on the preset.
manual.mchjong.entry.presets.page_2: One red dye crafts four Red Dora Dyes. Combine one with a 5m, 5p, or 5s tile to turn it into a red five, and use Undo Dye to change it back.
manual.mchjong.entry.presets.page_2.cont: Spare red fives can be stored in the box. The table picks a complete matching set automatically. Every tile type still needs four usable copies, red fives included.
manual.mchjong.entry.replays.exports: Riichi, MCR, Sichuan, and Taiwan replays can all be exported to Tenhou JSON format, saved in the replays/mchjong folder in your game directory.
manual.mchjong.entry.replays.name: Reviewing Matches
manual.mchjong.entry.replays.page_1: Open the record from the table screen with the Replays button, or run /mchjong replays. Only players who took part in the match can view its replays.
manual.mchjong.entry.replays.page_1.cont: Choose a hand, then use the timeline and playback buttons. The arrow buttons step through events; the decision buttons jump between choices.
manual.mchjong.entry.replays.page_2: Finished matches can be exported to JSON files and saved in the replays/mchjong folder in your game directory.
manual.mchjong.entry.replays.page_2.cont: Replay the entire match at any time to review discards, decision times, riichi declarations, and win evaluations. You can pause or exit the replay at any time.
manual.mchjong.entry.results.name: Results & Leaving
manual.mchjong.entry.results.page_1: When a hand ends, settlement shows the winning score and point transfers. Riichi mahjong also lists yaku, han, and fu. Multiple ron winners can be selected separately.
manual.mchjong.entry.results.page_1.cont: Use the continuation button to confirm the next hand. Ordinary tables pay with physical sticks. Open the side drawer, then drag sticks into the receiving player’s row.
manual.mchjong.entry.results.page_2: After settlement on an ordinary table, sweep the played tiles to the center. When the match ends, you return to the lobby and the dice and drawer sticks reset.
manual.mchjong.entry.results.page_2.cont: Solo practice against bots can always be quit in one click. Leaving a multiplayer match requires a unanimous vote, and the clock is paused while the vote is open.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi.declaration: In the online presets, declaring riichi requires at least 1,000 points and four tiles left in the live wall, or three tiles in three-player mahjong. The M.League and JPML A presets require one tile left. The WRC preset allows riichi with none left.
Competition presets allow the declaration even if you have fewer than 1,000 points. Temporary furiten ends when you next draw a tile. A concealed kan after riichi must leave your winning tile types unchanged. See $(l:riichi_presets)Preset Differences$(/l) for further restrictions.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi.name: Riichi, Calls & Furiten
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi.page_1: Declare Riichi when you have a closed hand in tenpai. Select and discard a tile, then place a 1,000-point riichi stick on the table.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi.page_1.conti: After riichi, you may not freely change your hand. You must discard each tile you draw unless you win or make a concealed kan or North extraction permitted by the rules.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi.page_1_conti: Chi forms a sequence using the previous player’s discard. Pon forms a triplet, and an open Kan forms a quad, using any opponent’s discard. These calls open your hand. Closed-hand-only yaku no longer count, and yaku subject to kuisagari lose one han.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi.page_2: If any tile you are waiting on is among your own discards, you are in discard furiten and cannot ron on any of your waits. Passing a winning discard gives you same-turn furiten.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi.page_2.conti: After riichi it lasts until the hand ends. You can still win by tsumo while in furiten. The red furiten badge on screen always tells you your current state.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.aborts: The online presets allow abortive draws. On your first draw, before any calls, you may declare Nine Terminals if you hold at least nine different terminal or honor tile types.
If all four players discard the same wind on their first turn without any calls, the hand ends in a Four Winds draw. The hand also ends if all four players declare riichi, or if multiple players make four kans in total.

After the fourth kan, its replacement draw and the following discard can still produce a win before the draw is declared. Four kans by one player do not end the hand. Abortive draws have no noten payment. The dealer repeats and the honba count increases by one.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.name: From Deal to Finish
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.page_1: Four-player Riichi mahjong uses four copies of each suited tile and seven honors, for a total of 136 tiles. Everyone receives 13 tiles.
The dealer takes one extra and discards first. Turns move counterclockwise. The last 14 tiles form the dead wall for replacement draws and dora indicators. Flowers are not used.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.page_2: Start with $(l:winning)Winning Hands$(/l), then read $(l:riichi)Riichi, Calls & Furiten$(/l). Normally you need one yaku han. Dora cannot supply it. Discard after Chi or Pon.
A kan uses four tiles as one group, so take a replacement. An added kan may be robbed. A concealed kan keeps your hand closed.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.page_3: The dealer repeats after winning, or after an exhaustive draw when tenpai. Otherwise the deal moves on. Draws and repeats add a honba. A nondealer win resets it.
Noten players share a 3,000-point payment to tenpai players. One receives 3,000, two receive 1,500 each, or three receive 1,000 each. All tenpai or all noten means nothing is paid.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.page_4: You normally play East and South, with four dealer positions per wind. Repeats add hands. The Mahjong Soul and Tenhou presets also offer East-only matches.
Online presets end after settlement if someone is below zero. Zero remains playable. See $(l:riichi_presets)Preset Differences$(/l) for final-dealer stops and extension.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.page_5: Each yaku’s explanation faces a tile example drawn with Kansai tile faces. Gaps separate groups, and + marks the winning tile. The example shows how that yaku is formed. Other yaku and dora may affect the hand’s total han.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_points.name: Fu & Points
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_points.page_: Regular hands start at 20 fu. Add ten fu for closed ron or two fu for tsumo. Pinfu tsumo stays at 20 fu without tsumo fu. Seven Pairs stays at 25 fu. Round other totals up to the next ten fu.

For suited tiles numbered 2–8, an open triplet scores 2 fu, a concealed triplet 4 fu, an open kan 8 fu, and a concealed kan 16 fu. Double these values for terminals and honors. A triplet completed by ron counts as open for fu. A dragon, seat-wind, or round-wind pair scores 2 fu.

A double-wind pair scores 4 fu in online presets and 2 fu in competition presets. Edge, closed, and single-tile pair waits add 2 fu. Two-sided and shanpon waits add none. An open hand with no fu beyond the base 20 fu is scored as 30 fu.
Below mangan, basic points = fu × 2^(han + 2). For ron, the discarder pays four times the basic points to a nondealer winner, or six times to a dealer winner.

For a nondealer tsumo, the dealer pays twice the basic points and each other player pays once. For a dealer tsumo, each opponent pays twice the basic points. Round each payment up to the nearest 100 points.
A nondealer’s 3 han 40 fu hand has 1,280 basic points. Ron pays 5,200 points. Tsumo collects 2,600 points from the dealer and 1,300 points from each other player.

Each honba adds 300 points to a ron payment, or 100 points to each tsumo payment. The winner also takes the riichi deposits. A nondealer’s 2-han Seven Pairs hand wins 1,600 points by ron. Its fixed 25 fu is not rounded up to 30.

Mangan applies at 5 han or when basic points reach 2,000. Ron pays 8,000 to a nondealer or 12,000 to the dealer. Haneman at 6–7 han pays 1.5 times mangan, baiman at 8–10 han pays twice mangan, and sanbaiman at 11–12 han pays three times mangan.

Normally, 13 or more han scores counted yakuman, worth four times mangan. The M.League preset instead caps these hands at sanbaiman. Natural yakuman do not add ordinary yaku or dora, but multiple natural yakuman can be combined.

Dora is the next tile after its indicator. Numbered suits run from 1 to 9 and back to 1. Winds cycle East–South–West–North. Dragons cycle White–Green–Red. Each dora adds 1 han. Each red five adds another 1 han, even if it is also the indicated dora.

A riichi winner also counts ura dora. Each kan adds a kan-dora indicator and its corresponding kan-ura indicator. The JPML A preset uses no ippatsu, ura dora, or kan dora. Dora adds han but cannot replace the yaku required to win.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.name: Preset Differences
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.page: The Mahjong Soul and Tenhou presets normally require at least 1 han from yaku. You may instead select a minimum of 2 or 4 han. Dora does not count toward this minimum, and the Tenhou preset also excludes ippatsu.

Natural yakuman qualify regardless of the minimum. You can change open tanyao, choose no red fives, three reds, or four reds, and select an East-only or East–South match without changing the preset name.
Other rule changes mark the rules as Custom. Switching presets keeps supported options and resets the other rules to that preset’s defaults.

The Mahjong Soul preset uses 25,000 starting and return points for four players, or 35,000 for three players. Uma, the placement bonus, is +15/+5/−5/−15 from first to fourth, or +15/0/−15 from first to third.
The Tenhou preset starts at 25,000 and returns at 30,000 for four players, or starts at 35,000 and returns at 40,000 for three. Uma is +20/+10/−10/−20 or +20/0/−20 respectively.
First place also receives oka, which is the sum of each player’s return-minus-start difference. Uma and oka are expressed in thousands of points.

Online presets allow bankruptcy endings, abortive draws, and match extensions. In the final hand, a dealer who would repeat ends the match if they are first and meet the target. Otherwise they repeat.

When the deal passes and nobody meets the target, play extends by at most one round. The target is 30,000 points for four players or 40,000 for three. The Mahjong Soul preset allows multiple ron winners.

The Tenhou preset ends the hand in a draw if three players claim ron. Only the Mahjong Soul preset counts Thirteen Orphans on a thirteen-sided wait, Four Concealed Triplets on a single-pair wait, Pure Nine Gates, and Big Four Winds as double yakuman.

The M.League preset starts at 25,000 points and returns at 30,000. Uma is +30/+10/−10/−30, with 20 oka for first place. It uses three red fives, ippatsu, ura dora, and kiriage mangan. Hands without a natural yakuman are capped at sanbaiman.

The JPML A preset starts and returns at 30,000. It uses no red fives, ippatsu, ura dora, or kan dora. Kiriage mangan is disabled, but 13 or more ordinary han may score four times mangan. Uma depends on how many players finish with at least 30,000 points.

The JPML A preset sets uma according to how many players finish with at least 30,000 points. Bonuses are listed from first to fourth. $(br)0 or 4 players: 0 / 0 / 0 / 0$(br)1 player: +12 / −1 / −3 / −8$(br)2 players: +8 / +4 / −4 / −8$(br)3 players: +8 / +3 / +1 / −12

Exactly 30,000 points counts toward this threshold. Final score is (final points − return points)/1000, plus uma and oka. In the JPML A preset, tied players share the uma for the places they occupy equally.

The WRC preset starts and returns at 30,000 points, with uma of +15/+5/−5/−15. It uses no red fives, but allows ippatsu, ura dora, kiriage mangan, and a counted fourfold-mangan limit. Renhou pays the higher of mangan or the ordinary hand’s score.

Do not add its five han to other yaku or dora. The M.League, JPML A, and WRC presets use head bump. Only the ron claimant nearest the discarder in turn order wins. They have no bankruptcy ending, abortive draws, nagashi mangan, extension, or final-dealer stop.

Normal dealer repeats still apply. Online presets break score ties by initial seat order, while competition presets share tied placement bonuses. The JPML A and WRC presets leave final riichi deposits unclaimed.

Kiriage mangan scores 4 han 30 fu or 3 han 60 fu as mangan. A double-wind pair is worth 4 fu in online presets and 2 in competition presets. A concealed kan after riichi must preserve the winning tile types.

Competition presets also require the same possible group arrangements, and the JPML A preset forbids losing a yaku. Big Three Dragons and Big Four Winds use responsibility payments. Competition presets also apply them to Four Kans.

On self-draw, the responsible player pays the full amount covered by responsibility. If another player discards the winning tile, those two players usually split that amount equally. Rule details specify which honba and combined-yakuman payments are covered.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_sanma.name: Three-player Riichi
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_sanma.page_1: Three-player mahjong removes the 2 through 8 of characters, leaving 108 tiles, and does not allow Chi. Nondealers start with 13 tiles and the dealer with 14. The seats are East, South, and West, so each round has three dealer positions.

You may keep North in your hand as an ordinary tile, or extract it and draw a replacement. Each extracted North adds 1 bonus han. Extraction keeps the hand closed but does not provide a yaku. A 1-of-characters indicator makes the 9 of characters dora, and a 9 makes the 1 dora.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_sanma.page_2: Extracting North cancels ippatsu. Another player may win on the extracted tile if their hand meets the winning conditions. Winning on its replacement tile does not by itself count as Rinshan kaihou.
North extractions and kans count toward the same replacement limit. On a self-draw, each opponent pays the same amount as in four-player mahjong. Nobody pays the missing fourth player’s share.
For example, a nondealer’s mangan self-draw collects 4,000 points from the dealer and 2,000 from the other player. The total noten payment on an exhaustive draw is 2,000 points.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.name: Yaku
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_1: $(bold)Riichi$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Declare riichi with a closed hand in tenpai and pay a 1,000-point deposit. After declaring, you may no longer freely change your hand. Riichi does not score in addition to Double Riichi.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_10: $(bold)White dragon$()$(br)1 han$(br2)A triplet or kan of White dragons scores one han, even in an open hand. In Little Three Dragons, the two dragon triplets or kans each also score their own dragon yaku.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_11: $(bold)Green dragon$()$(br)1 han$(br2)A triplet or kan of Green dragons scores one han, even in an open hand. In Little Three Dragons, the two dragon triplets or kans each also score their own dragon yaku.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_12: $(bold)Red dragon$()$(br)1 han$(br2)A triplet or kan of Red dragons scores one han, even in an open hand. In Little Three Dragons, the two dragon triplets or kans each also score their own dragon yaku.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_13: $(bold)Rinshan kaihou$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Win by self-draw on the replacement tile drawn after a kan. Your hand may be open. A replacement drawn for North extraction does not by itself qualify.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_14: $(bold)Chankan$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Win by ron on the fourth tile another player adds to an open triplet to declare a kan. Your hand may be open. Kokushi musou has a separate exception for robbing a concealed kan.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_15: $(bold)Haitei raoyue$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Win by self-draw on the last tile drawn from the live wall. Your hand may be open. A kan replacement tile does not qualify.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_16: $(bold)Houtei raoyui$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Win by ron on the discard made after the last ordinary draw from the wall. Your hand may be open.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_17: $(bold)Chiitoitsu$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Form seven different pairs in a closed hand. Four identical tiles cannot count as two pairs. The hand is always worth 25 fu. Do not score this yaku together with Ryanpeikou.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_18: $(bold)Sanshoku doujun$()$(br)2 / 1 han$(br2)Form the same sequence in each of the three suits. This scores two han with a closed hand, or one han with an open hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_19: $(bold)Ittsu$()$(br)2 / 1 han$(br2)Form the sequences 123, 456, and 789 in the same suit. This scores two han with a closed hand, or one han with an open hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_2: $(bold)Double riichi$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Declare riichi on your first discard, before anyone has made a call. Your hand must be closed. Double Riichi replaces ordinary Riichi rather than adding to it.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_20: $(bold)Chanta$()$(br)2 / 1 han$(br2)Every group and the pair must contain a terminal or honor tile. The hand must include at least one sequence and at least one honor tile. This scores two han closed, or one han open.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_21: $(bold)Toitoi$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Form four triplets or kans and a pair. Your hand may be open. A Seven Pairs hand does not qualify.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_22: $(bold)Sanankou$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Form three concealed triplets or kans. The remaining group may be open. A triplet completed by ron does not count as concealed.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_23: $(bold)Sanshoku doukou$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Form a triplet or kan of the same number in each of the three suits. Your hand may be open.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_24: $(bold)Sankantsu$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Form three kans, whether open or concealed, and complete the remaining group and pair.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_25: $(bold)Shousangen$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Form triplets or kans of two dragons and a pair of the third dragon. Your hand may be open. The two dragon groups also score their own dragon yaku.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_26: $(bold)Honroutou$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Use only terminals and honors. Your hand may be open. A four-group-and-pair hand also scores All Pungs. A seven-pair hand also scores Seven Pairs.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_27: $(bold)Honitsu$()$(br)3 / 2 han$(br2)Use tiles from one numbered suit together with honor tiles. This scores three han closed, or two han open.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_28: $(bold)Junchan$()$(br)3 / 2 han$(br2)Every group and the pair must contain a terminal tile. The hand must include at least one sequence and no honor tiles. This scores three han closed, or two han open. Do not also score Chanta.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_29: $(bold)Ryanpeikou$()$(br)3 han$(br2)Form two pairs of identical sequences in a closed hand. Together with the pair, these make the complete winning hand. Do not also score Iipeikou or Seven Pairs.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_3: $(bold)Ippatsu$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Win within one uninterrupted circuit of turns after declaring riichi. Calls, kans, and North extraction cancel ippatsu. The JPML A preset does not use this yaku.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_30: $(bold)Chinitsu$()$(br)6 / 5 han$(br2)Use tiles from a single numbered suit, with no honors. This scores six han closed, or five han open. Do not also score Half Flush.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_31: $(bold)Blessing of Man$()$(br)Mangan$(br2)In the WRC preset, a nondealer qualifies by winning on a discard before their first draw and before anyone has made a call. Score the hand normally, then compare that result with mangan and use the higher value. Do not add other yaku or dora to the mangan awarded for this condition.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_32: $(bold)Nagashi mangan$()$(br)Mangan$(br2)At an exhaustive draw, all your discards must be terminals or honors, and none may have been claimed. Normally, you must not have made any open calls. The Tenhou preset allows them. Receive the payments for a mangan self-draw, without honba bonuses or riichi deposits.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_4: $(bold)Menzen tsumo$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Win by self-draw with a closed hand. Concealed kans do not open the hand. This yaku can combine with Pinfu.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_5: $(bold)Pinfu$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Form four sequences and a pair that is not a value honor, in a closed hand, and win on a two-sided wait. The hand is worth 20 fu on self-draw or 30 fu on ron.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_6: $(bold)Tanyao$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Use only numbered tiles from two through eight. Open hands qualify by default. If open tanyao is disabled, the hand must be closed.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_7: $(bold)Iipeikou$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Form two identical sequences of the same suit in a closed hand. Do not add this yaku when scoring Ryanpeikou.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_8: $(bold)Seat wind$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Form a triplet or kan of your seat wind. Your hand may be open. If your seat wind is also the round wind, the group scores two han in total.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.page_9: $(bold)Round wind$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Form a triplet or kan of the round wind. Your hand may be open. If it is also your seat wind, score both yaku.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.name: Yakuman
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.page: $(bold)Kokushi musou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)In a closed hand, collect one of each of the thirteen terminal and honor tiles, plus a duplicate of one of them to form a pair. An ordinary single-tile wait scores one yakuman.
$(bold)Ryuuiisou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Use only the 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 of bamboo and Green dragons. Your hand may be open, and it does not need to contain a Green dragon.
$(bold)Chuuren poutou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)In a closed hand, form 1112345678999 in one suit, plus one more tile of that same suit. You must not have declared any kans.

$(bold)Pure chuuren poutou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Before the winning tile arrives, hold exactly 1112345678999 in one suit, waiting on all nine numbers. This scores double yakuman in the Mahjong Soul preset and one yakuman in the other presets.
$(bold)Suukantsu$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Form four kans, whether open or concealed, and a pair. You must complete the winning hand. Declaring the fourth kan alone does not win.
$(bold)Tenhou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)As dealer, win with your initial dealt hand. The hand must be closed, with no intervening calls.
$(bold)Chiihou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)As a nondealer, win on your first self-draw before anyone has made a call. Your hand must be closed.

$(bold)Kokushi musou thirteen-sided wait$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Before the winning tile arrives, hold one of each of the thirteen terminal and honor tiles, waiting on any of those thirteen kinds. This scores double yakuman in the Mahjong Soul preset and one yakuman in the other presets.

$(bold)Suuankou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Form four concealed triplets or kans in a closed hand. If you are waiting to complete one of two pairs as a triplet, you must win by self-draw. A triplet completed by ron does not count as concealed.

$(bold)Suuankou tanki$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)With all four concealed triplets or kans already complete, win on the single-tile wait that completes the pair. Ron is allowed. This scores double yakuman in the Mahjong Soul preset and one yakuman in the other presets.

$(bold)Daisangen$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Form a triplet or kan of each of the three dragons. Your hand may be open. Do not add the ordinary dragon yaku. A player who supplies the discard for your third exposed dragon group may become liable for payment.
$(bold)Shousuushii$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Form triplets or kans of three winds and a pair of the fourth wind. Your hand may be open.

$(bold)Daisuushii$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Form a triplet or kan of each of the four winds. Your hand may be open. This scores double yakuman in the Mahjong Soul preset and one yakuman in the other presets. A player who supplies the discard for your fourth exposed wind group may become liable for payment.
$(bold)Tsuuiisou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Use only honor tiles. Your hand may be open. A closed hand of seven honor pairs also qualifies.
$(bold)Chinroutou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Use only numbered ones and nines to form four triplets or kans and a pair. Your hand may be open.
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.name: Seating & Preparation
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.page_1: Right-click a stool to sit down. The first player to sit becomes the host. Select the variant in the lobby sidebar, then configure its player count and rules in Match settings.
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.page_1.cont: Invite friends or fill empty seats with Bots. Once all seats have occupants, click the seat-assignment button.
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.page_2: Ordinary tables deal concealed wind tiles to decide seats. Automatic tables assign them directly. Sit at your assigned stool and click Ready.
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.page_2.cont: Auto-seating is on by default. The match starts when everyone is sitting in the right seat and ready, and the equipment matches the rules.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.name: Fan Patterns
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_1: $(bold)All pungs$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Form four pungs or kongs and a pair. Your hand may be open. A Seven Pairs hand does not also score All Pungs.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_10: $(bold)Last-tile win$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Win by self-draw on the final tile, or on the discard that follows that draw. This fan is not included when calculating ready-hand payments at an exhaustive draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_2: $(bold)Golden single wait$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)After forming four pung or kong melds, wait with your one remaining tile to complete the pair. Also add one fan for All Pungs.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_3: $(bold)Full flush$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)Use tiles from only one numbered suit. Your hand may be open. This can combine with Seven Pairs, Roots, or All Pungs. The payment cap still applies.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_4: $(bold)Seven pairs$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)Form seven pairs without making calls or declaring kongs. Four identical tiles may count as two pairs and also score a Root. Do not also score All Pungs.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_5: $(bold)Root$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Use all four copies of a tile without declaring a kong. Each such set scores one fan. In the MIL preset, declared kongs score under Kong instead.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_6: $(bold)Kong$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)In the MIL preset, each declared kong adds one fan to the winning hand. This is separate from the immediate payment for declaring a kong. The T/TFMJ preset scores this under Root instead.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_7: $(bold)Win after kong$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Win by self-draw on the replacement tile drawn after a kong. Calculate the base value with this extra fan, then add the usual one-point self-draw bonus to each opponent’s payment.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_8: $(bold)Win on a Discard After a Kong$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Win on another player’s discard immediately after a kong. Any kong refund or transfer is settled separately. In the MIL preset, this also applies when you win on an added kong declared with a kong replacement tile.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.page_9: $(bold)Robbing a kong$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Win on the fourth tile another player adds to a pung to declare a kong. Their original pung remains. Do not also score Win on a Discard After a Kong for the same win.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.name: Sichuan Play
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.notati: Each pattern’s explanation faces its example, which uses Sichuan tile faces. Spaces separate groups, + marks the winning tile, and / separates melds from concealed tiles.
The listed fan value is for that pattern alone, not the whole hand. Patterns marked closed require a closed hand. Other ordinary patterns allow open melds.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.page_1: Sichuan is played by four players with 108 suited tiles, with no honors or flowers. You receive 13 tiles, or 14 as the dealer. Choose one suit to void after the deal.
You must clear every tile of it before winning. Discard void-suit tiles first. There is no chow. You can pung and kong only the other suits.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.page_2: In the MIL preset, choose your first discard privately when choosing your void suit. You must discard that tile on your first turn. If your hand contains no tiles of the void suit, you do not need to choose a first discard.
All players reveal their void suits together. The chosen discards remain secret. The T/TFMJ preset only asks you to choose a void suit. Neither preset uses the three-tile exchange.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.page_3: Win with four groups and a pair, or Seven Pairs. No minimum fan is required. Four identical tiles may count as two pairs.
In blood battle, winners retire while everyone else keeps playing. Three winners or wall exhaustion ends the hand. Several players may win one discard. Its supplier pays each separately.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.page_4: Passing a win blocks a later win of the same or lower fan, even after declining self-draw. Drawing again or becoming not ready clears it.
Compare fan after the cap. Two hands both capped at three fan remain equal even if one has more raw fan.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.page_5: Zero, one, two, and three fan pay a base value of 1, 2, 4, and 8 points. Three fan is the cap. A discarder pays that value. Each still-active opponent pays value plus one point on self-draw.
A two-fan Full Flush takes four points on a discard. With all four active, self-draw takes five points from each opponent, or fifteen points in total. After one retires, it takes ten points.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.page_6: The first winner deals next. If the first win has several winners on one discard, its supplier deals. With no winner, the dealer stays. Both presets normally play eight hands and rank cumulative scores.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.sichua: Four copies of the same tile count as two pairs and a root.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_payments.pa: A concealed kong collects two points from each active opponent. A discard kong collects two points from its supplier. Immediately adding the drawn fourth tile to a pung collects one point from each active opponent.
A delayed added kong collects nothing. Kong income is separate from winning fan. Draw a replacement tile after a kong. A robbed added kong does not complete or collect a kong payment.

If a player’s discard immediately after a kong lets an opponent win, the MIL preset refunds only that player’s last kong payment to its original payers. The T/TFMJ preset instead transfers all income from that consecutive run of kongs to the winners.
For example, if the kongs earned five points and two players win, each receives three points. The discarder supplies the missing one point. Pay the winning hands separately.
In the MIL preset, four identical tiles declared as a kong score Kong. Four used without declaring a kong score Root. The T/TFMJ preset scores both as Root. Each set adds one fan.
If another player wins on an added kong made with a kong replacement tile, the MIL preset treats the win as Win on a Discard After a Kong. The kong is completed but earns no kong payment.

The T/TFMJ preset treats it as Robbing a kong, leaving the original pung intact. The East and West walls have 14 stacks each in the MIL preset. The South and North walls have 14 each in the T/TFMJ preset.
When the wall runs out, players who have not yet won have their hands checked. Each player who is not ready pays every eligible ready player the highest base value their hand could achieve.
Do not include bonuses for winning on a kong replacement or the last tile. Players who are not ready must also refund any kong income they still retain.

For example, if two ready hands are worth two and eight points, a player who is not ready pays them two and eight points respectively. Players who have already won are excluded. If three players win before the wall runs out, there are no ready-hand checks or kong refunds.
A player who still holds void-suit tiles when the wall runs out is a passive Flower Pig. Treat their hand as not ready and refund their kong income.
An active Flower Pig violation called by the referee deducts 24 competition points, prevents further wins, and requires kong income to be refunded. The 24-point penalty is not paid to anyone.

A penalized player who is ready neither receives nor pays ready-hand payments. Completed transfers of kong income to winners are not reversed. Custom rules can change the fan cap, self-draw bonus, kong payments, and match length.
manual.mchjong.entry.stock.name: Dice & Point Sticks
manual.mchjong.entry.stock.page_1: Ordinary tables need dice and point sticks of your own. Craft two dice from bone meal, white dye, and black dye. Use a stonecutter to turn one bone block into 24 blank point sticks.
manual.mchjong.entry.stock.page_1.contin: Dye blank sticks white, blue, yellow, red, or black to make 100-, 1,000-, 5,000-, 10,000-, and −10,000-point sticks.
manual.mchjong.entry.stock.page_2: A standard 25,000-point start calls for 17 sticks per seat. Give each player ten 100s, four 1,000s, two 5,000s, and one 10,000. A 30,000 start adds one 5,000, and a 35,000 start adds one 10,000.
manual.mchjong.entry.stock.page_2.contin: Sticks can be stored in the box or the side drawer. If the bankruptcy-ending rule is disabled, keep one black negative stick per seat ready for negative balances.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.name: Sixteen-tile Play
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.notatio: Each pattern’s explanation faces its example, which uses Taiwanese tile faces. Spaces separate groups, + marks the winning tile, and / separates melds from concealed tiles.

In flower examples, / separates different players’ tiles. The listed tai value is for that pattern alone, not the whole hand. Patterns marked closed require a closed hand. Other ordinary patterns allow open melds.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.page_1: Taiwanese mahjong is played by four players. The Pocket preset adds eight flowers to the ordinary 136 tiles. The Southern preset uses no flowers. You can play with built-in computer opponents as long as at least one human participates.
Deal four tiles to each player in each of four rounds, then give the dealer one extra tile. The dealer starts with 17 tiles and discards first. A regular winning hand needs five groups and a pair. The fourteen-tile Seven Pairs and Thirteen Orphans hands are not used.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.page_2: Replace the opening flowers in rounds, starting with the dealer. If a replacement is another flower, wait until every player has finished that round before replacing it.
During play, reveal any flower you draw and take replacements from the end of the wall until you draw an ordinary tile. You may chow only the previous player’s discard, but may pung or kong any opponent’s discard.
Winning takes priority over pung or kong, which take priority over chow. If several players claim a win, only the first in turn order after the discarder wins.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.page_3: After a chow or pung, discard before taking another action. Every kong requires a replacement draw. An added kong can be robbed, but a concealed kong cannot. Declaring a kong does not itself earn an immediate payment.
Declare ready by discarding a tile that leaves your hand in tenpai. Afterward, you must discard each tile you draw unless you win. You cannot chow, pung, or kong. No deposit is required, and you may win without declaring ready.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.page_4: Passing a win temporarily prevents both discard wins and self-draw wins. Drawing a tile alone does not clear the restriction. It ends when you discard a tile that was not among your waits immediately before that draw or call, or when you complete an added kong.
By default, leave sixteen tiles in the wall, plus one more for each completed kong. A fixed sixteen-tile reserve is also available. Reserved tiles cannot be drawn, even for flower or kong replacements. If no legal replacement remains, the hand ends in a draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.page_5: Play through sixteen dealer positions across the East, South, West, and North rounds. A dealer win or exhaustive draw keeps the dealer and adds one repeat. A nondealer win passes the deal to the next player and resets the repeat count. The final North dealer may also repeat.
Scores start at zero. Exhaustive draws have no ready-hand payments. There are no abortive draws, bankruptcy endings, or automatic stops after a dealer win. See $(l:taiwan_payments)Flowers, Base & Tai$(/l) and $(l:taiwan_tai)Tai Patterns$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.taiwan: Five groups and a pair make seventeen tiles.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_payments.pag: A discard win charges the discarder. Self-draw charges all three opponents. Each pays base + per-tai value × payable tai. Defaults are base one point and one point per tai.
The Pocket preset adds one dealer tai when either party is dealer, plus two tai per repeat. The Southern preset omits the one dealer tai but keeps two tai per repeat.
In the Pocket preset, a nondealer self-draw worth three tai during one repeat collects four points from each nondealer and seven points from the dealer (1 + 3 + 1 + 2), for a total of fifteen points.
The Southern preset caps hand tai at four before dealer/repeat additions. Its dealer winning eight raw tai during one repeat collects 1 + 4 + 2 = 7 points from each liable payer.
Collect all eight flowers for Eight Flowers, or hold seven while another player holds the eighth for Seven Robbing One. Both score eight tai without a regular 17-tile winning shape.

All three opponents pay for Eight Flowers. Only the player holding the eighth flower pays for Seven Robbing One. When you draw your seventh or eighth flower, complete the replacement draw before the flower win is decided.

If an opponent draws the eighth flower, Seven Robbing One takes effect immediately, before their replacement draw. During the deal, flower wins are decided after everyone finishes all flower replacements.

Flower wins are automatic, even when passing on a win would prevent an ordinary win. If a replacement tile also completes a regular winning hand, add that hand’s tai. For Seven Robbing One, only the player with the eighth flower pays the flower tai.
All three opponents pay the regular self-draw tai. Each payer owes the base amount only once. Pocket rules score Seat Flowers, Flower Sets, and Single Wait.

A self-draw on either a flower or kong replacement tile can score Replacement Win. Southern rules use no flowers and do not score Single Wait. Only kong replacements qualify for Replacement Win, and the hand’s tai are capped at four.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.name: Tai Patterns
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_1: $(bold)Heavenly hand$()$(br)24 tai$(br2)The dealer wins with the dealt hand after completing flower replacements, before anyone has called chow, pung, or kong. Do not add Concealed Self-Draw, Concealed Hand, Self-Draw, or Replacement Win.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_10: $(bold)Full flush$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Use tiles from just one numbered suit, with no honors. The hand may be open. Do not add Half Flush.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_11: $(bold)Small four winds$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Form pungs or kongs of three winds and use the fourth wind as the pair. Complete the hand with two more sets. The hand may be open.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_12: $(bold)Big three dragons$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Form a pung or kong of each of the three dragons. The hand may be open. Do not add tai for the individual dragon sets.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_13: $(bold)Five concealed triplets$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Form five concealed pungs or kongs. Do not add Three Concealed Triplets or Four Concealed Triplets, but do add All Triplets. A pung completed by the winning discard does not count as concealed.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_14: $(bold)Four concealed triplets$()$(br)5 tai$(br2)Form four concealed pungs or kongs. The remaining set may be open. Do not add Three Concealed Triplets.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_15: $(bold)All triplets$()$(br)4 tai$(br2)Form five pungs or kongs and a pair. The hand may be open. All Triplets can be added to Five Concealed Triplets, but not to All Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_16: $(bold)Half flush$()$(br)4 tai$(br2)Use tiles from one numbered suit together with honors. The hand may be open.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_17: $(bold)Small three dragons$()$(br)4 tai$(br2)Form pungs or kongs of two dragons and use the third dragon as the pair. The hand may be open. Do not add tai for the individual dragon sets.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_18: $(bold)Pinfu$()$(br)2 tai$(br2)Form five sequences and a pair of numbered tiles, with no honors or flowers, and win on a discard. The hand may be open. Under Pocket rules, a two-sided wait is not required, and Single Wait may also be scored.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_19: $(bold)Three concealed triplets$()$(br)2 tai$(br2)Form three concealed pungs or kongs. The remaining sets may be open. A pung completed by the winning discard does not count as concealed.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_2: $(bold)Earthly hand$()$(br)16 tai$(br2)A nondealer wins on their first draw, before anyone has called chow, pung, or kong. Do not add Concealed Self-Draw, Concealed Hand, or Self-Draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_20: $(bold)Concealed hand$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win without having called chow, pung, or an exposed kong. Concealed kongs are allowed. Winning by self-draw with a concealed hand scores three tai for Concealed Self-Draw instead of one tai each for Concealed Hand and Self-Draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_21: $(bold)Self-draw$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Draw the winning tile yourself. The hand may be open. If your hand is concealed, score the three-tai Concealed Self-Draw instead.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_22: $(bold)Concealed self-draw$()$(br)3 tai$(br2)Win by self-draw with a concealed hand. Concealed kongs are allowed. Do not add Concealed Hand or Self-Draw separately. Concealed Self-Draw is not added to Heavenly Hand or Earthly Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_23: $(bold)All from others$()$(br)2 tai$(br2)Expose all five sets through chow, pung, or kong calls, then complete the pair with the winning discard. A hand containing a concealed kong does not qualify.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_24: $(bold)Half from others$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Expose all five sets through chow, pung, or kong calls, then complete the pair by self-draw. Do not also score All From Others.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_25: $(bold)Replacement win$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win by drawing a replacement tile after a kong. Pocket rules also allow a win on a flower replacement tile. Southern rules allow only kong replacements. Self-draw tai may also be scored.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_26: $(bold)Last draw$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win by drawing the last available tile from the wall. Tiles reserved at the end of the wall are not available to draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_27: $(bold)Last discard$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win on the discard made after the last available tile has been drawn from the wall.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_28: $(bold)Robbing a kong$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win on the fourth tile that another player adds to an exposed pung to make a kong. Concealed kongs cannot be robbed.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_29: $(bold)Declared ready$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win after declaring ready. You may declare ready with an open hand. Heavenly Ready and Earthly Ready replace this one-tai award.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_3: $(bold)Human hand$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)A nondealer wins on another player’s first discard, before the dealer’s second discard and before anyone has called chow, pung, or kong. Do not add Concealed Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_30: $(bold)Single wait$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Your hand must wait on just one tile type. Edge waits, closed waits, and pair waits can all qualify. The number of remaining copies does not determine this award. Southern rules do not score Single Wait.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_31: $(bold)Red dragon$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Form a pung or kong of Red dragons. The set may be open. Do not add this tai to Big Three Dragons or Small Three Dragons.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_32: $(bold)Green dragon$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Form a pung or kong of Green dragons. The set may be open. Do not add this tai to Big Three Dragons or Small Three Dragons.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_33: $(bold)White dragon$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Form a pung or kong of White dragons. The set may be open. Do not add this tai to Big Three Dragons or Small Three Dragons.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_34: $(bold)Flower set$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Collect all four seasons or all four plants to score one tai per complete set. Pocket rules also score any matching Seat Flowers in the set. Do not add these ordinary flower awards to a flower win.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_35: $(bold)Round wind$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Form a pung or kong of the round wind. The set may be open. If the round wind is also your seat wind, score both awards.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_36: $(bold)Seat wind$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Form a pung or kong of your seat wind. The set may be open. Seat winds are assigned East, South, West, and North relative to the current dealer.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_37: $(bold)Seat flower$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Flower numbers one through four correspond to East, South, West, and North. Score one tai for each flower matching your seat wind. Do not add Seat Flowers to a flower win.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_4: $(bold)Heavenly ready$()$(br)16 tai$(br2)The dealer declares ready with their first discard, before anyone has called chow, pung, or kong, and later wins. Do not add Concealed Hand or Declared Ready.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_5: $(bold)Earthly ready$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)A nondealer declares ready with their first discard during an opening turn uninterrupted by chow, pung, or kong, and later wins. Do not add Declared Ready.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_6: $(bold)Eight flowers$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Collecting all eight flowers automatically wins the hand without a regular winning shape. Do not add Seat Flower or Flower Set. If the replacement tile also completes a regular winning hand, score that hand separately.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_7: $(bold)Seven robbing one$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)If you hold seven flowers and another player holds the eighth, you win with Seven Robbing One and that player pays. Do not add Seat Flower or Flower Set. If your replacement tile also completes a regular winning hand, score that hand separately.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_8: $(bold)Big four winds$()$(br)16 tai$(br2)Form a pung or kong of each of the four winds, plus one more set and a pair. The hand may be open. Seat Wind and Round Wind may also be scored.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.page_9: $(bold)All honors$()$(br)16 tai$(br2)Use only honor tiles. The hand may be open. Do not add All Triplets.
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.name: Crafting a Tile Set
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.page_1: Planks, bone blocks, quartz blocks, calcite, glass, and amethyst blocks all stonecut into 16 blank tiles each. Nine blocks give exactly 144 blanks, a full set.
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.page_1.contin: Craft the box from leather, wooden slabs, a chest, and an iron nugget, then right-click it while holding it to open.
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.page_2: Put exactly 136 or 144 blanks with matching material and backs into the tile slots. One of each black, red, green, blue, and white dye crafts Mahjong Dye.
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.page_2.contin: Insert it into the dye slot, pick the face preset, and click Apply to print the whole set. The 144-tile style includes eight flower tiles.
manual.mchjong.entry.winning.name: Winning Hands
manual.mchjong.entry.winning.page_1: A standard winning shape has four groups and one pair, totaling 14 tiles if no kans have been declared. A group can be a sequence (three consecutive numbers of one suit), a triplet (three identical tiles), or a declared kan (four identical tiles).
manual.mchjong.entry.winning.page_1.cont: Honors can form triplets or kans, but not sequences. Seven Pairs and Thirteen Orphans are exceptions. Winning on your own draw is tsumo. Winning on another player's discard is ron.
manual.mchjong.entry.winning.page_2: To win, your hand needs at least one yaku on top of the shape (the minimum-han requirement). Start with closed riichi, All Simples, and the triplet yaku of your seat wind, round wind, and dragons.
manual.mchjong.entry.winning.page_2.cont: Dora adds han but never counts toward the minimum. For practice, the host can enable Open Hands. Turn on Tenpai Hints in Room settings before starting to see your waits and remaining copies computed from the visible tiles in real time.
manual.mchjong.landing: Learn how to set up tables, craft items, and use the controls. Read the rules of Riichi mahjong, MCR, Sichuan, and Taiwan mahjong.$(br2)Browse the chapters below or search by keyword. Every entry is unlocked from the start.
manual.mchjong.name: Mahjong Handbook
manual.mchjong.recommend.text: Install the optional Patchouli mod to read the Mahjong Handbook in-game. Please download the file matching your Minecraft version and mod loader.
mchjong.ponder.table_equipment.text_1: Put the tiles your rules need into the box. Use 136 for four players or 108 for three, all with matching material, backs, and face preset. Spare tiles may stay in the box.
mchjong.ponder.table_equipment.text_2: Right-click the table to open its storage. It holds up to two boxes.
mchjong.ponder.table_equipment.text_3: Right-click the table with a cloth in hand to drape it. With the cloth down and a full set ready, you can start preparing a match.
mchjong.ponder.table_equipment.text_4: Open the side drawer to store every stick denomination and pay players manually during settlement.
mchjong.ponder.table_equipment.text_5: While waiting, move boxes in and out through the storage screen. Keep both hands empty and sneak-right-click the tabletop to retrieve the cloth.
mchjong.ponder.table_placement.text_1: Leave a clear 3 × 3 area for the table, with nothing blocking the space above.
mchjong.ponder.table_placement.text_2: Place the table in the center of the area. Its rim reaches into the surrounding blocks.
mchjong.ponder.table_placement.text_3: Put one stool two blocks from the center on each side you play on.
mchjong.ponder.table_placement.text_4: Both ordinary and automatic tables use this compact layout.
mchjong.ponder.table_playing.text_1: Right-click a stool to sit down and open the table screen. Right-click the stool again while seated to reopen it.
mchjong.ponder.table_playing.text_2: Pick a three- or four-player preset in the lobby, then have everyone click Ready.
mchjong.ponder.table_playing.text_3: On ordinary tables, sweep the loose tiles to shuffle, drag stacks in front of you to build the wall, then drag tiles from the wall into your hand.
mchjong.ponder.table_playing.text_4: Automatic tables shuffle, build walls, deal, and draw all by themselves.
mchjong.ponder.table_playing.text_5: Click a table tile to discard it. The screen lists the chi, pon, kan, riichi, and win options available right now.
mchjong.ponder.table_playing.text_6: Close the screen and you can look around while staying seated. Press sneak to stand up.
mchjong.ponder.workshop_dyeing.text_1: Use a mixer and basin to dye two stacks of tiles, two boxes of tiles, or one of each with a single dye. Each full stack or box counts as one. For example, two boxes and one blue dye turn the backs of both sets blue.
mchjong.ponder.workshop_dyeing.text_2: Only the backs change. Faces, red fives, material, names, sticks, and dice stay untouched. Glass tiles turn into stained glass.
